attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter. The examples he cites from other users are separate from this sentence.

semantics.note: The 'will see' wording is about the future, but its factual parts describe the product at launch. 'Exciting' is a subjective judgment, not a testable fact.

contract.note: Reading it as being about o1-preview at launch, treating 10-20 s as an ordinary range, and not scoring the excitement judgment are all fair, ordinary readings.

evidence.note: An independent launch-week test found a 14 s average displayed thinking time, inside the stated range. It covers only one task.
OpenAI's launch system card reports nonzero o1-preview hallucination rates on simple fact questions. Lower than GPT-4o does not mean the errors are gone.
OpenAI's claim of reasoning gains, plus its admission that features were missing. This does not settle a subjective judgment about excitement.

reviews.rationale: The two testable parts hold. An independent launch-week measurement averaged 14 s, inside the 10-20 s range, though only for one task. OpenAI's own launch evaluations show o1-preview still made basic factual errors. The 'lack of exciting features' part is opinion and is not scored. OpenAI's improvement claims do not contradict the factual parts.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated firmly as 'I believe'.

semantics.note: Present-tense description. 'Subprime AI crisis' is a metaphor; the testable core is thousands of integrations at unstable, unprofitable prices.

contract.note: Tying profitability to provider pricing matches the context. Requiring a service-level cost basis is an added interpretation, but it is applied evenly to support and contradiction.

evidence.note: AWS says tens of thousands of customers use Bedrock. This fits the scale of 'thousands' but says nothing about price stability or profitability.
A rough estimate of a 75% gross margin on the API, excluding training and salaries. It is unverified and uses a narrower cost basis, so it cannot decide the claim.
The analysts' 2026 retrospective says their margin estimates remain unconfirmed and unrefuted.

reviews.rationale: The evidence fits the scale of thousands of business users. It does not show whether provider prices were materially unstable or below cost in Q2 2024. The only margin evidence is an unverified estimate on a narrow cost basis that points the other way, and it is not decisive.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary sentence. The phrase 'we may never make a profit' paraphrases OpenAI's investor warning, but the forecast is his.

semantics.note: Mixes a present observation with firm 'will' forecasts and sets no deadline.

contract.note: Reading 'burning money' as net cash burn, and requiring that later funding terms include the warning, are reasonable readings. A decline in a completed year as early contradiction fits the plain sense of 'only burn more'.

evidence.note: OpenAI raised new money in October 2024. This says nothing about cash burn or whether the warning was in the terms.
Unverified report of first-half 2025 burn and a full-year target. These are not comparable completed annual results.
Court filing quoting the 2019 warning. It does not show the terms of later funding rounds.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was set, and there is no comparable series of completed annual cash-burn figures. Later funding is shown, but not that later agreements kept the warning. Nothing triggers an early contradiction, and the evidence does not settle the forecast.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: A firm 'are not going to' forecast that keeps 'magically', so it denies that spending alone creates capabilities. It is partly rhetorical.

contract.note: The contract treats 'magically' as emphasis, which risks a stronger reading than he gave. Its causal-link requirement partly keeps his 'money alone' sense. Support can never be shown because the forecast has no end date.

evidence.note: Anthropic describes its new computer-use skill as applying existing abilities. Nothing links it to the stated investment or shows that spending caused it.

reviews.rationale: This forecast has no deadline. The packet has no investment records matching the stated scope, and nothing causally links spending to new LLM abilities. The computer-use evidence neither proves nor rules out the claim, so the early-contradiction rule is not met.
